text:
maria: quick sync? noticed a spike in per-sku token cost after yesterday's routing tweak. numbers look off vs baseline.
aj: saw that too — rough magnitude?
devon: ~18% increase on small-ctx requests routed to sku-v2. sample: 2026-03-20 22:00-23:00 UTC.
sasha: is it token burn or classifier/extract overhead? dashboard shows spike in token-level + cache miss rate.
maria: cache-hit dropped from 87% -> 62% for that sku chain.
lucas: that aligns with the sticky-routing fallback change we rolled. we started preferring regional-sku with lower cache affinity.
bill: did we change sampling or telemetry that could make token accounting appear higher?
devon: no sampling change. query we used to compute unit econ:

```
SELECT sku, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost) as cost
FROM token_ledger
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-20T22:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-20T23:00:00Z'
GROUP BY sku;
```

maria: console panel shows cost/spike concentrated in short-seq (<128) requests.
aj: short seqs are sensitive to batching heuristics and kernel selection — could be running on a different model variant that has worse per-token efficiency for short contexts.
sasha: UX question: should we expose a per-sku cache-affinity column in the econ table? would help triage.
lucas: +1. also need a quick flag to run a canary that pins old routing policy for the sku to compare.
bill: ops-bot, can we rollback routing policy for sku-132 to pre-change as a canary?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: request received — started canary rollback for sku-132 to routing-policy v1. ETA ~3m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria: while we wait, can someone dump the per-node kv cache hit rates?
devon: grabbing now — back in 90s with small window. attaching snippet.

```
node,kv_hit_rate
node-01,0.91
node-02,0.89
node-03,0.63
```

sasha: node-03 is the one serving most sku-v2 traffic in eu-west. maybe imbalance.
aj: what about quota interplay? if quotas tripped we might have been routed to fallback skus with no warm cache.
lucas: quota logs show a few soft-throttles around 22:10 on tenant T-77, which drives sku-v2. those throttles triggered fallback routing.
bill: OK that explains cache cold path. mitigation: revert fallback aggressiveness, or add prewarm for fallback skus.
maria: for the dashboard: propose adding a diffs sparkline (pre/post-policy) and a column for cache-affinity + sample rate.
sasha: will sketch a console mock. simple UX: toggle 'compare routing policies' and show two sparklines + % delta.
aj: for telemetry we should tag the token ledger rows with routing_policy_id so diffs are straightforward
maria: great. add backlog tasks: (1) roll back fallback aggressiveness for sku-132 (devon/bill), (2) console mock (sasha), (3) tag ledger rows and run diff job for last 7d (aj), (4) add per-node kv heatmap to econ panel (lucas).
devon: ack, starting rollback monitor.

sasha: quick note — when we add tag, keep event size small; we already pay emit costs for each attempt. maybe sample flag for historical replay.
aj: yes — do not increase prod event size; use a derived tagging job that backfills metadata into the econ table.
maria: thanks team. ops-bot: confirm rollback completion?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback completed for sku-132. traffic split restored to 95% v1 / 5% v2. :white_check_mark:

maria: re-run diff job tomorrow morning and loop in billing if numbers still diverge.
lucas: will add alert rule: if cache-affinity drops >15% post-rollout then auto-pause aggressive fallbacks.
bill: adding oncall playbook note.

maria: closing this thread, will file RFC for routing-policy telemetry and console diff UX. thanks everyone :tada:
